title: Safe Handling of Chemicals

competencies.text: Apply best practices for handling, storage, and disposal of chemicals.
Create a table showing saltwater/wastewater effects on local ecosystems and recommend minimization strategies.

days.title: Reading Hazard Symbols
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will apply best practices for handling, storing and disposing of chemicals, and create a table of saltwater and wastewater effects on local ecosystems with ways to reduce them.

⚠️ GHS Pictograms

The Globally Harmonized System (GHS) uses red-bordered diamond symbols so anyone, in any country, can recognize a hazard.

PictogramHazardExamples
💀 Skull and crossbonesAcute toxicity (can kill)Rat poison, some pesticides
🔥 FlameFlammableAlcohol, LPG, paint thinner
🧪 CorrosionBurns skin, eyes, metalsMuriatic acid, drain cleaner
❗ Exclamation markIrritant, harmfulDetergents, some cleaners
🫁 Health hazardLong-term harm (organs, cancer)Some solvents and pesticides
🐟 EnvironmentToxic to aquatic lifeMotor oil, many pesticides

📣 Signal Words

DANGER means a severe hazard; WARNING means a less severe one. Always read the precautionary statements and first-aid section before using a product.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: A muriatic acid bottle shows a pictogram of liquid eating into a hand and a metal bar. What does it warn?

choices.label: It is corrosive to skin and metal
It is flammable and catches fire
It is harmful only to fish in rivers
It is a gas stored under pressure

scenario.explanation: The corrosion pictogram warns that the chemical can burn skin and eyes and damage metals.

scenario.text: Which signal word indicates the MORE severe hazard?

choices.label: DANGER
WARNING
CAUTION
NOTICE

scenario.explanation: Under GHS, DANGER is used for the more severe hazards and WARNING for less severe ones.

scenario.text: A paint thinner can shows a flame pictogram. Where should it be used and kept?

choices.label: Away from open flames and heat sources
Beside the kitchen stove for easy reach
Inside a closed car under the hot sun
Next to candles so it stays warm

scenario.explanation: The flame pictogram means flammable. Vapors can ignite, so keep it away from flames, sparks and heat.

days.title: Handling and Storage
days.content:
🦺 Safe Handling

  • Read the label before opening. Wear gloves and eye protection when the label says so.
  • Work in a well-ventilated area. Never smell chemicals directly — waft the air toward your nose if needed.
  • When diluting acid, add acid to water, slowly — never water to acid, which can boil and splash.
  • Never mix cleaners (bleach + ammonia or acid releases toxic gases).

📦 Safe Storage

RuleReason
Keep in original labeled containersLabel gives contents, hazards and first aid
Never use food or drink bottlesChildren may drink them by mistake
Store acids apart from bases and bleachIncompatible chemicals can react if they leak
Keep flammables away from heatPrevents fires
Store high and locked, away from foodProtects children and food

RA 6969 (Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act) regulates toxic chemicals and hazardous waste in the Philippines.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each practice or term to its reason or meaning. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.why: The water absorbs the heat safely.
Children may mistake chemicals for drinks.
Fresh air lowers the amount of vapor you breathe.

match.right: Protect skin and eyes from contact
Law on toxic substances and hazardous waste
match.why: It is enforced by DENR's Environmental Management Bureau.

match.right: Safe way to detect a smell
match.why: Never sniff directly from the container.

days.title: Disposal and Wastewater
days.content:
🗑️ Proper Disposal

  • Use up products as directed, or give them to someone who can use them.
  • Never pour pesticides, motor oil, paint or solvents into drains, canals or soil.
  • Bring used oil, batteries and hazardous waste to collection points or treatment facilities; follow barangay and LGU schedules.
  • Keep empty pesticide containers out of reuse — never use them for water or food.

🌊 Saltwater and Wastewater Effects

SourceEffect on local ecosystemsWays to minimize
Saltwater intrusionSalty wells; rice fields failLimit pumping, rainwater harvesting, mangroves, salt-tolerant crops
Detergent wastewaterEutrophication; fish killsPhosphate-free detergents, septic tanks, treatment
Untreated factory wasteToxic metals build up in fishTreatment plants, DENR permits, monitoring
Oil and greaseCoats gills and feathers; blocks oxygenGrease traps, used-oil collection

Some toxic metals like mercury and lead bioaccumulate: they build up in organisms and become more concentrated up the food chain — reaching people who eat contaminated fish.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Decide what to do in real situations. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A family has expired pesticide and leftover motor oil. What is the BEST way to dispose of them?

choices.label: Bring them to a hazardous-waste collection point
Pour them down the kitchen drain with hot water
Bury them in the backyard garden beside the plants
Mix them together and burn them in an open pit

scenario.explanation: Hazardous waste must go to proper collection or treatment. Drains, soil and open burning spread pollution.

scenario.text: A student wants to dilute concentrated acid for a cleaning task. What is the correct method?

choices.label: Slowly pour the acid into the water
Quickly pour the water into the acid
Mix equal amounts all at once quickly
Heat the acid first, then add water

scenario.explanation: Adding acid to water lets the larger amount of water absorb the heat. Water added to acid can boil and splash.

scenario.text: Fishers notice fish from a river near a mining area have high mercury levels, and people who eat them get sick. What explains this?

choices.label: Mercury builds up in organisms along the food chain
Mercury evaporates from the fish when they are cooked
Fish make their own mercury when the water is warm
Mercury is only harmful when it is touched by hand

scenario.explanation: Mercury bioaccumulates: small organisms absorb it, fish eat many of them, and the concentration rises up to humans.

scenario.text: A restaurant drains its cooking grease directly into the canal. What is the MOST likely effect?

choices.label: Grease coats the water and blocks oxygen exchange
Grease feeds the fish and makes them grow faster
Grease cleans the canal by dissolving the garbage
Grease turns into fresh water after a few days

scenario.explanation: Oil and grease form a film that reduces oxygen entering the water and can coat gills and feathers.

scenario.text: A coastal barangay's rice fields have become too salty after years of over-pumping. Which plan BEST addresses BOTH cause and effect?

choices.label: Limit pumping and plant salt-tolerant rice
Pump more water to wash the salt away faster
Add more fertilizer to make the rice grow taller
Cover the rice fields with plastic sheets for a year

scenario.explanation: Limiting pumping reduces further intrusion (cause); salt-tolerant rice lets farming continue (effect).

days.title: Making a Safer Community
days.content:
🏘️ A Household Chemical Safety Plan

  1. Inventory — list every chemical at home with its pictograms.
  2. Store — group by hazard (flammables, corrosives, pesticides), high and locked, in original containers.
  3. Use — follow labels, wear PPE, ventilate, never mix cleaners.
  4. Dispose — use collection programs; never drains, soil or burning.
  5. Prepare — know first aid and keep emergency numbers near the phone.

🛟 First Aid Reminders

  • Skin or eye contact: rinse with plenty of running water for 15–20 minutes; remove contaminated clothing.
  • Inhaled fumes: move to fresh air.
  • Swallowed: do not induce vomiting unless told by a health professional; bring the label to the clinic.

🧠 Thinking Like a Scientist

Good decisions weigh benefits and risks. A chemical that helps (pesticide protects crops) can also harm (poisons fish). Using the right amount, the right way, and disposing of it properly keeps the benefit while lowering the risk.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What does the GHS skull-and-crossbones pictogram mean?

choices.label: Acute toxicity — can cause death
Flammable — catches fire easily
Corrosive — damages skin and metal
Irritant — causes a mild skin rash

escape.explanation: The skull and crossbones marks chemicals that can cause serious harm or death even in small amounts.

escape.text: Why must acids and bases be stored apart?

choices.label: Leaks could react and release heat or gas
They have the same color and get confused
Acids make bases lose their strong smell
Bases freeze when placed beside acids

escape.explanation: Incompatible chemicals can react violently if containers leak or break, releasing heat or harmful gases.

escape.text: Which Philippine law regulates toxic substances and hazardous waste?
escape.explanation: RA 6969 covers toxic substances and hazardous and nuclear wastes. RA 9003 is solid waste, RA 9275 clean water, RA 8749 clean air.

escape.text: Bleach splashes onto your arm. What should you do FIRST?

choices.label: Rinse with running water for 15–20 minutes
Wipe it off with a dry cloth and keep working
Apply vinegar to neutralize the bleach on skin
Cover it with a bandage to keep air away

escape.explanation: Plenty of running water removes and dilutes the chemical. Adding other chemicals can cause more harm.

escape.text: Which practice BEST prevents children from swallowing household chemicals?

choices.label: Store them high, locked, in labeled original containers
Store them in clear soft-drink bottles for easy viewing
Keep them under the sink beside the dish soap
Remove the labels so children are not curious

escape.explanation: Locked, high storage in original labeled containers keeps chemicals out of reach and clearly identified.

escape.text: Which is the BEST way to reduce detergent pollution in a nearby creek?

choices.label: Use phosphate-free detergent and proper drainage
Use twice as much detergent so clothes get clean faster
Wash clothes directly in the creek water
Add salt to the wash water before draining

escape.explanation: Phosphate-free detergents and proper drainage or septic systems reduce the nutrients that cause eutrophication.
